qc.overall: Oathsplitter is a strong, buildable concept. The long slot is genuinely open (background shows through it), the bridge below the fork and the twin tines are present, the blade faces are quiet, and the vermilion crescent guard with its amber gem and gold root frame is the clear focal point. It reads instantly even when downsampled to 96 px. Nothing breaks an invariant. The fixes are a mirrored guard (the horns don't match), a stronger bridge flush with the rail faces, a cleaner guard-to-ferrule stack on the pommel side, and material painting that reads less like marble or cracked stone. The palette also needs pulling back toward the brief's less saturated ivory, gold and charcoal under neutral light. The front and back are fully hidden, so the modeler has to settle thickness, the rear face and how the parts join using the resolutions below.

invariants.requirement: "a two-handed greatsword with a long, actual opening inside the blade and two substantial points at the tip" (sec 4)
invariants.evidence: Slot runs from the blade root at about 45% of total length to a bridge at about 80%, so it is roughly 33% of total length and about 9:1 length to width. Two tines continue past the bridge to separate points at about (1470,20) and (1485,135).

invariants.requirement: "Its silhouette should be immediately recognizable from the split form" / "easiest member of the set to identify in silhouette"
invariants.evidence: At 96x64 px and in a thresholded silhouette, the slot, the fork notch and both tips stay readable, as do the crescent horns. Sunbound (solid blade) and Warlink (two cleavers plus a chain) are clearly different shapes.

invariants.requirement: "The opening is empty three-dimensional space, visible from front and back, with inner faces and bevels... Do not fake the opening with a black polygon"
invariants.evidence: Pixels in the slot (e.g. (906,437) #2B272B) match the background (#252225), so it is a real opening, not black paint. The upper rail's inner wall shows as a shaded band (#60412F at (885,405)) along the whole slot, which reads as depth. The back view and the lower rail's inner wall can't be seen from this angle.

invariants.requirement: "Keep thick structural rails on both sides"
invariants.evidence: Measured across the blade, the lower rail is about 81-90 px wide and the upper rail about 88-113 px. The slot is only about 60 px, so each rail is wider than the opening. Side and bevel planes show on the rail edges (e.g. #8B7467 at (963,525)).

invariants.requirement: "a substantial bridge below the fork, so the opening and split tip remain coherent parts of one forceful blade"
invariants.evidence: A bridge is present at about (1150-1230, 210-300) and joins the rails. It is short along the blade (about 65 px, less than one rail width) and looks recessed: its face sits below the rail faces, with chamfered sides. That makes it read more like a strut than a solid block.

invariants.requirement: "Use broad warm ivory/steel blade faces"
invariants.evidence: The faces are broad and quiet with no runes or gems. The ivory is a saturated peach-tan (median #E9C8A8) rather than #E5DDC7. The cool pearl-steel note appears only in the tip shading (#89828A, #A08B80).

invariants.requirement: "vermilion crescent-like guard with a clear center connection and a small number of large, swept points"
invariants.evidence: Two large crescent horns (tips at about (520,360) and (880,745)) and two small rear spurs, with a gem-and-bezel boss at the center (about (582,620)). The guard's red median is #9D312A, with lit faces at #D94D41.

invariants.requirement: "The guard must have believable depth and a readable overlap with the blade base"
invariants.evidence: Chamfers on the horns suggest thickness, and the gem bezel overlaps the seam. But the blade root mostly butts against the red body along a diagonal line, and the pommel side of the guard is a lumpy stack of red blocks around (420-500, 520-700). It's not clear whether the guard wraps the blade or the blade sits on top.

invariants.requirement: "Add restrained aged-gold inlay or a simple directional motif where it supports the existing forms"
invariants.evidence: A cusped gold frame around the slot root points up the blade, and there are crescent inlays on each horn, a gem bezel, spacer rings and pommel ridges. The amount is restrained, but the gold is more saturated and brassy (median #B67B3F) than #9D7950.

invariants.requirement: "Provide a charcoal wrapped, genuinely usable two-handed grip"
invariants.evidence: The wrap is about 22% of total length, roughly 7 grip diameters (a 52 px diameter over about 368 px), which fits two hands. The crossing leather bands read as grippable. The color is a warm brown-black (median #231D1A) rather than cool charcoal #24282D.

invariants.requirement: "Separate the hand area from the guard and pointed pommel. The handle should not read as a second blade."
invariants.evidence: A red ferrule with a gold spacer ring sits at each end of the wrap (around (465,690) and (170,910)). The pommel is a faceted red-and-gold point. The handle is round and dark, nothing like the blade.

invariants.requirement: "Start with a blade occupying roughly two thirds of total weapon length"
invariants.evidence: From the guard's front edge to the tips is about 60% of the pommel-to-tip length (about 62% including the blade root under the guard). That's slightly under two thirds but within the stated guide.

invariants.requirement: "Place low amber heat along selected inner edges or a narrow channel near the opening. In idle, preserve clear dark space through the slot."
invariants.evidence: Amber (#F58D28, hot #FFAB47) appears only at the U-shaped end of the slot near the root, about (640-670, 560-600), and in the gem. The slot stays dark and clear, but there is no defined channel along the inner edges for the equip ignition to travel along.

invariants.requirement: "The energy... must not fill the entire opening with an opaque wall"
invariants.evidence: No glow across the slot. The bloom is small and local at the root.

invariants.requirement: Sec 3: "Leave meaningful quiet surfaces. Concentrate detail at guards, connection points..."
invariants.evidence: Detail is concentrated at the guard, the blade root frame and the pommel. The rails carry only a few silhouette scallops and steps.

invariants.requirement: Sec 3: "Ivory metal should still read as forged material... Avoid indiscriminate noisy grunge"
invariants.evidence: The bevel transitions are clean and the tips are crisply faceted, but cloudy mottling over the faces (e.g. (900-1100, 300-450)) reads as marble or bone more than forged metal.

invariants.requirement: Sec 3: "Red elements are substantial structural pieces, enamel, or forged housings with visible thickness"
invariants.evidence: Chamfers show thickness, but painted fissure lines on the guard (around (500,470), (650,690) and (700,780)) read as cracked stone or rock.

invariants.requirement: Sec 3: "Reserve the brightest highlights for important edges and focal materials"
invariants.evidence: The amber gem is the most saturated point, as intended. But the largest bright area is a broad glare on the lower rail's face mid-blade (#FBE0BF at (944,496)), while the coplanar upper rail at the same point is #CAAE94.

invariants.requirement: Sec 7: front, rear, side surfaces with intentional thickness; credible joints
invariants.evidence: There is a single three-quarter view only. Thickness is hinted by the rail side planes, the inner wall and the tip facets. The rear face, side profile, guard thickness and blade-to-guard joint are not shown (see ambiguities).

invariants.requirement: Family and house-style continuity (concept briefs "Shared family"; closest continuation of the original Iop blade)
invariants.evidence: It keeps the original's ivory blade, red guard, long slot, twin points and forward-curving horns, but makes them heavier, as the brief asks. Ivory, red, gold rings and a dark wrap match Sunbound and Warlink, and the lighting is consistently from the top.

invariants.requirement: No third-party watermark or logo copied from references
invariants.evidence: No marks or logos anywhere in the image.

issues.where: Crescent guard horns: upper horn tip about (520,360), lower horn tip about (880,745)
issues.problem: The guard is not mirrored about the blade centerline. The upper horn reaches about 275 px out from the centerline and barely sweeps forward (its tip is at about 40% of total length). The lower horn reaches about 250 px but sweeps about 125 px further toward the tip (about 47.5%). A modeler would have to guess which one is correct.
issues.fix: Build the guard symmetric. Use the lower horn's forward sweep for both: each tip ends at about 47% of length and about 0.155 x total length out from the centerline, so the full span is about 0.31 x total length. Mirror the gold crescent inlays the same way.

issues.where: Bridge below the fork, about (1150-1230, 210-300)
issues.problem: The bridge is shorter along the blade than one rail is wide (about 65 px against about 85-90 px), and it appears sunk below the rail faces with chamfered flanks. At a distance or lower LOD it reads as a thin strut, which weakens the 'one forceful blade' requirement.
issues.fix: Make the bridge flush with the rail faces, at 85-100% of rail thickness, and at least one rail width long along the blade. Fillet it into the fork crotch above and the slot end below with radii of about 0.4 x rail width. Keep a single chamfer ring that continues the rail bevels.

issues.where: Pommel side of the guard, around the ferrule and neck block, about (420-500, 520-700)
issues.problem: The red ferrule, a red neck block, the guard body and two small rear spurs overlap as lumpy chunks with dark gaps between them. It's unclear how many parts there are and how the grip ferrule seats into the guard.
issues.fix: Define four clean parts. (1) Guard body: a crescent plate with a raised central boss. (2) Red neck collar, about 1.5 x grip diameter, about 0.02 x total length. (3) Gold spacer ring. (4) Red ferrule. Give the guard body exactly two small mirrored rear spurs and a smooth convex back contour.

issues.where: Grip wrap, about (200-460, 690-910), against the background
issues.problem: The wrap's value almost matches the background (median #231D1A against #252225). In the 96 px icon only the faint highlights on the wrap bands keep the handle visible. Its hue is also warm brown rather than the cool charcoal swatch, and slightly darker and browner than the Sunbound (#2C272B) and Warlink (#30272A) grips.
issues.fix: Set the wrap albedo to about #2E2F33 (cool charcoal), with band-edge highlights at about #57534F and gaps at about #17181B, and lower roughness slightly on the band crowns. Use the same wrap material on all three weapons. For inventory icons, add a rim light or use a mid-value backplate.

issues.where: Blade faces, especially mid-blade on both rails, (850-1150, 280-500)
issues.problem: Cloudy marble-like mottling across the broad faces makes the ivory read as stone or bone rather than forged metal. It works against sec 3's forged material and its warning against indiscriminate noisy grunge.
issues.fix: Paint broad directional gradients: lighter toward the outer edges, darker toward the slot's inner edges, a subtle warm-to-cool shift toward the tips (to #C9CDD0), crisp bright bevel lines, and a few edge nicks near the tips and the bridge. Use a low-amplitude hammered normal rather than cloud noise.

issues.where: Red guard body and horns: fissure lines near (500,470), (650,690) and (700,780)
issues.problem: The crack lines make the vermilion read as cracked rock or lava. The brief calls for enamel or forged housings.
issues.fix: Remove the through-cracks. Use enamel-style edge chipping on the horn tips and boss corners, slight value variation on the plates, and a darker deep-red (#702D27) in the recesses. Keep any wear at the edges.

issues.where: Overall palette, sampled
issues.problem: The colors drift from the swatches. The ivory median #E9C8A8 is peachier and more saturated than #E5DDC7. The gold median #B67B3F is brassier than aged gold #9D7950. The amber core #F58D28 is more orange than #F5AB46. The red is fine (median #9D312A, light #D94D41, shadow #862A22). Part of the drift is the warm studio lighting.
issues.fix: Author the base color under neutral light: blade face about #E3D8C3, inner slot walls about #B9A58C, tip steel blending to #C9CDD0, gold #9D7950 with highlights about #C4A26E, amber emissive #F5AB46 with an orange falloff. Check against a grey backdrop.

issues.where: Rail outer contours and tines, about (885,285) and the tips at (1470,20) and (1485,135)
issues.problem: There are small left/right asymmetries. The upper rail has an extra shoulder step at about 64% of length with no counterpart on the lower rail, and it measures 88-113 px wide against 81-90 px for the lower rail. The upper tine is wider (about 58 px against 35 px at 95% of length) and about 50 px longer, while the lower tine hooks inward more. The outer scallops at about 76-78% of length are roughly mirrored.
issues.fix: Mirror both rails about the slot centerline. Keep the paired outer scallops just before the bridge. Either add the shoulder step to the lower rail or remove it from the upper one (adding it is recommended for rhythm). Make the tines equal length with the same slight inward hook.

issues.where: Upper vs lower rail faces at the same point along the blade, (862,370) vs (944,496)
issues.problem: The lighting is inconsistent: the lower rail carries a strong glare (#FBE0BF) while the coplanar upper rail is much darker (#CAAE94). This suggests the rails are tilted differently and puts the largest highlight mid-blade instead of at the focal area.
issues.fix: Model the rail faces as coplanar flats and let the bevels carry the highlights. Don't bake that glare into the base color. Let the guard connection and inner edges hold the strongest accents.

issues.where: Amber heat at the slot root, about (640-670, 560-600)
issues.problem: The energy exists only as a glow at the U-shaped end plus the gem. There is no defined inner-edge channel for the brief's equip ignition to travel along toward the twin points.
issues.fix: Add a narrow recessed channel (about 8-10% of rail width) on both inner slot bevels, running from the root to the bridge, with a separate emissive mask. Idle: only the root third glows, at low intensity. Equip: a pulse travels up the channel to the bridge and fades toward the tips. The slot interior stays dark.

issues.where: Gem bezel at the guard center, about (582,620)
issues.problem: The diamond bezel straddles the seam where the red guard meets the gold blade-root frame, overlapping the frame's lower corner. Its attachment is ambiguous (guard part or blade part).
issues.fix: Make the gem part of the guard boss: a rhombic gold bezel set into the boss, centered on the blade axis, with the blade root seated just behind it. Use a faceted amber crystal with low or no idle emission so it doesn't compete with the slot heat.

ambiguities.where: Rear face of the whole weapon
ambiguities.ambiguity: It's unknown whether the gold root frame, horn inlays, gem and scallops repeat on the back.
ambiguities.resolution: Make the blade, guard and pommel symmetric about the blade plane (mirror front to back). Use a double-sided gem (a bipyramidal crystal through the boss) or a matching gem on the back. Hidden-face detail should never just stop at the centerline.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Only thin side bands are visible, so the true thickness and edge sharpness are unknown.
ambiguities.resolution: Use a flattened hexagonal section per rail: central flat about 55-60% of rail width, thickness about 0.35-0.4 x rail width. Taper the outer bevels to a blunted edge about 25% of the center thickness. The inner (slot) edges are square walls with a 45-degree chamfer of about 15% of rail width, which also hosts the amber channel. Tines use a diamond section with a central ridge.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Only the upper rail's inner wall is visible, and the depth treatment at the U-shaped end isn't defined.
ambiguities.resolution: Flat inner walls the full rail thickness deep, chamfered to both faces, with a rounded U at the root (radius = half the slot width). Paint them darker (#8A7462 to #6A5040), not black.

ambiguities.ambiguity: The bridge appears recessed, so it's unclear whether it is thinner than the rails.
ambiguities.resolution: Build it flush and 90-100% as thick as the rails, with a concave top forming the fork crotch and a flat bottom forming the slot end. It must not be a separate floating bar.

ambiguities.ambiguity: It's unclear whether the blade root sits on top of the guard, butts against it, or passes through it.
ambiguities.resolution: The blade root (the area inside the gold cusp frame) passes through a slot in the guard body. The boss wraps the front and back of the root by about 0.02 x total length. A hidden tang runs through the grip to the pommel. Make the guard body about 1.4 x blade center thickness at the boss, tapering to about 0.5 x at the horn tips.

ambiguities.ambiguity: It's unclear whether the horns bend toward or away from the viewer.
ambiguities.resolution: Keep both horns in the guard plane (perpendicular to the blade, coplanar with it), swept forward in-plane only, with beveled edges and recessed gold crescent channels on both faces.

ambiguities.ambiguity: The pommel-side contour has one or two indistinct small points.
ambiguities.resolution: Exactly two small mirrored rear spurs, each about 0.25 x horn length, pointing back toward the grip at about 45 degrees.

ambiguities.ambiguity: It's unclear whether the wrap is modeled geometry or texture, and whether the grip is round or oval.
ambiguities.resolution: Slightly oval grip (about 1.12:1, long axis in the blade plane), with a 6-8 turn helical wrap modeled as a shallow relief (about 4-6% of diameter) or as a baked normal map on a low-poly cylinder. Taper the grip about 5% thicker near the guard.

ambiguities.ambiguity: It's unclear whether the pommel has three or four sides and where the gold sits.
ambiguities.resolution: A four-sided faceted pyramid, rotated 45 degrees to the blade plane. Red enamel panels on each face, gold strips along the four ridges and a gold base band, then a red collar and a gold spacer ring before the wrap.

strengths: The split silhouette survives downsampling to 96 px: slot, fork notch, both tips and the crescent horns all stay readable.
The opening is truly empty (slot pixels match the background), and a shaded inner wall gives it depth instead of a painted line.
The structure matches the brief: two thick rails, each wider than the slot, a bridge below the fork, and two separate tips.
The blade faces are quiet, and the detail sits at the guard connection, the blade root and the pommel, as section 3 asks.
Clear three-way value grouping: light ivory blade, mid-value red guard and pommel, dark grip. A small saturated amber accent marks the focal point.
The guard uses a few large swept points rather than many spikes, and its forward-curving horns continue the original house-style guard.
The hand zone is clearly framed by red ferrules and gold spacer rings, and the pointed pommel is distinct. The grip is long enough for two hands and never reads as a second blade.
Strong family match with Sunbound and Warlink (ivory, vermilion, gold rings, wrapped grips) while staying the most distinctive silhouette of the three.
The idle amber is restrained and the slot stays dark.
No copied watermark or logo.

parts.name: Blade_Main (single mesh: root, two rails, bridge, two tines)
parts.material: Warm ivory forged metal (base about #E3D8C3, cool steel blend toward the tips)
parts.shape: Broad root into two parallel rails with a long open slot, a flush bridge, then a fork notch and two diamond-section tines. Mirrored outer contour with one shoulder step per rail at about 64% and a crescent scallop per rail at about 76%.
parts.approx_proportion: Blade runs from about 40% to 100% of total length L (0.60 L long). Width at root about 0.14 L. Each rail about 0.052 L wide. Slot about 0.036 L wide, from 0.45 L to 0.78 L. Bridge from 0.78 to 0.82 L (at least one rail width long). Tines about 0.18 L long. Rail thickness about 0.019 L at the center flat, edges about 0.005 L.

parts.name: Blade_RootFrame_Gold
parts.material: Aged gold, shallow raised inlay
parts.shape: Cusped, ogee-shaped frame around the slot's U-end, its points directed up the blade. Front and back.
parts.approx_proportion: Spans about 0.40-0.50 L along the blade. Strip width about 0.008 L, relief about 0.002 L.

parts.name: Slot_EnergyChannel (VFX mask / emissive inset)
parts.material: Amber emissive (#F5AB46 core) on a dark recessed groove
parts.shape: Narrow groove on both inner slot chamfers, from the root U to the bridge. Separate emissive mask or thin separate mesh.
parts.approx_proportion: Groove width about 0.004 L, depth about 0.002 L, from 0.45 to 0.78 L.

parts.name: Guard_Crescent
parts.material: Vermilion enamel / forged red (#B93C2B lit, #702D27 recesses)
parts.shape: Symmetric crescent plate perpendicular to the blade. Two large horns swept forward in-plane, two small rear spurs, a raised central boss wrapping the blade root, beveled edges.
parts.approx_proportion: Span about 0.31 L. Axial depth at center about 0.08 L (about 0.33-0.41 L along the length), horn tips at about 0.47 L. Thickness about 1.4 x blade thickness at the boss, about 0.5 x at the horn tips.

parts.name: Guard_HornInlays_Gold (x4: two per face)
parts.material: Aged gold
parts.shape: Crescent channels following the inner curve of each horn
parts.approx_proportion: Each about 0.07 L long and about 0.012 L wide at the widest point, shallow relief.

parts.name: Guard_Gem + Bezel
parts.material: Amber faceted crystal in an aged-gold rhombic bezel
parts.shape: Rhombic table-cut gem set into the boss on the blade axis. Double-sided or mirrored on the back.
parts.approx_proportion: Long axis about 0.045 L, short axis about 0.03 L. Bezel rim about 0.005 L. Protrudes about 0.006 L from the boss.

parts.name: Guard_NeckCollar + GoldSpacer + Ferrule_Upper
parts.material: Vermilion collar and ferrule, aged-gold spacer ring
parts.shape: Stacked cylindrical rings with chamfered edges
parts.approx_proportion: Together about 0.03 L along the length, diameter about 1.4-1.5 x grip diameter.

parts.name: Grip_Wrap
parts.material: Charcoal leather wrap (#2E2F33 base, lower sheen than the metals)
parts.shape: Slightly oval cylinder with a 6-8 turn helical wrap relief, about 5% thicker near the guard.
parts.approx_proportion: About 0.19 L of wrap (roughly 0.10-0.29 L), diameter about 0.031 L. About 7 diameters long, enough for two hands. Tune to the avatar rig.

parts.name: Ferrule_Lower + GoldSpacer
parts.material: Vermilion ring and aged-gold spacer
parts.shape: Chamfered rings between the wrap and the pommel
parts.approx_proportion: About 0.025 L along the length, diameter about 1.35 x grip.

parts.name: Pommel_Point
parts.material: Vermilion enamel panels with aged-gold ridge strips and a base band
parts.shape: Four-sided faceted pyramid pointing away from the blade, rotated 45 degrees to the blade plane
parts.approx_proportion: About 0.075 L long (0-0.075 L), max width about 0.05 L.

sampled_palette: Grip wrap median / band highlight / gaps: #231D1A / #44352F / #1A140F
Recommended neutral-light albedo targets: ivory #E3D8C3, inner walls #B9A58C, tip steel #C9CDD0, vermilion #B93C2B, deep red #702D27, aged gold #9D7950, wrap #2E2F33, amber emissive #F5AB46
build_spec.notes: Proportions are fractions of total length L, measured along the pommel-tip-to-blade-tip axis of the image (1686 px). They are design ratios; set the absolute scale against the Roblox avatar. Mirror everything left/right about the slot centerline and front/back about the blade plane. The concept's asymmetries in the guard horns, rail steps and tine lengths are generation artifacts and should not be reproduced. Seven parts are enough to cover the material and VFX split: Blade_Main, the root-frame and horn gold inlays (can be merged into one gold mesh), Guard (body plus collars), Gem, Grip_Wrap, Pommel, plus an emissive mask for the slot channel. Suggested pivot: the center of the upper half of the grip on the blade axis. VFX attachments: one at the slot root, one at the bridge, one per tine tip. Painting: broad gradients plus crisp bevel highlights instead of the concept's marble mottling, and enamel edge chips instead of rock cracks. Keep the slot see-through from every angle; check with effects off from the front, rear, side and three-quarter views. Budget guide: 4k-12k triangles.

checks.claim: Issue: guard horns not mirrored (upper horn sweeps forward less than lower horn)
checks.reason: Measured along the PCA weapon axis (L=1720 px), the upper horn tip is at t=0.424 and the lower at t=0.484, about 0.06 L (~100 px) apart. The upper horn hooks back hard, while the lower one is a long forward-swept crescent. The lateral reach differs less than claimed (0.158 L vs 0.153 L, ~272 vs ~263 px, not 275 vs 250), and the forward offset is ~100 px rather than 125. The core claim holds.

checks.claim: Issue: bridge is short and recessed, reads as a strut
checks.reason: On the bridge crop (1080-1520, 150-360) it is a waisted, hourglass strut with concave ends. Its face sits below the rail faces, with chamfered walls visible on both sides. The silhouette is one solid segment only from t~0.775 to ~0.81 (about 0.035 L, ~60 px), against a rail width of 0.048-0.053 L (83-91 px).

checks.claim: Issue: pommel-side guard stack is lumpy and unclear
checks.reason: In the guard-rear crop, the red ferrule, a thin gold ring, a chamfered red neck block, and the guard body with its upper rear spur stack up as separate cracked blocks with dark gaps between them (around 420-520, 520-720). Part count and seating are not clear.

checks.claim: Issue: grip wrap value nearly matches background; warm brown not cool charcoal
checks.reason: My masked median for the wrap is #241A17 against a background of #252225. The value is almost identical and the hue is warm brown. In the 96x64 downsample the handle survives only as a faint brown line. Minor nit: the wrap is one overlapping helical strap, not 'crossing bands'.

checks.claim: Issue: cloudy marble-like mottling on blade faces
checks.reason: The mid-blade crop (780-1180, 300-560) shows soft cloudy blotches across both rail faces. The house-style ref has smoother graded faces. It's a texture-painting issue, not geometry, so medium severity is at the high end of fair.

checks.claim: Issue: crack/fissure lines on red guard read as rock
checks.reason: Fine dark through-lines are visible on the upper plate near (500,470), on the lower plate near (650,690)/(700,780), and on the neck block. They read as stone fissures rather than enamel chips. The same treatment shows up on the pommel panels.

checks.claim: Issue: palette drift (ivory peach, gold brassy, amber orange; red fine)
checks.reason: Independent masked medians: ivory #E6C8AB, gold #A66E3F, red #942E26. Ivory and gold drift as described. The red is darker than the #B93C2B swatch, so calling it 'fine' is slightly generous. Their albedo target fixes that anyway.

checks.claim: Issue: upper rail has extra shoulder step at ~64% with no counterpart; tines unequal
checks.reason: The lower rail does have a matching but much smaller step: a notch at (1007,482), which projects to t=0.627, the same station as the upper shoulder at (885,285), also t=0.627. The real problem is a size mismatch, not a missing feature. The tine part is confirmed: the tips are at t=0.998 vs 0.970 (~48 px), and at t=0.94 the upper tine is ~53 px wide vs ~29 px for the lower.

checks.claim: Issue: inconsistent rail lighting (lower rail glare vs darker upper rail)
checks.reason: I sampled #FDE2C2 at (944,496) and #CAAE95 at (862,370). In the mid-blade crop the lower rail is visibly brighter along most of its length. Severity is low, as stated.

checks.claim: Issue: amber exists only at slot root and gem, no channel
checks.reason: The glow sits only at the U-end of the slot (~640-680, 560-600) and in the gem. Neither inner edge has a continuous emissive line or groove up toward the bridge.

checks.claim: Issue: gem bezel straddles guard/root-frame seam
checks.reason: The rhombic bezel at about (582,620) sits across the diagonal seam between the red body and the ivory/gold root frame, overlapping the frame's lower cusp. Ownership is ambiguous.

checks.claim: Invariant partial: opening is true 3D space
checks.reason: Slot pixels (#2C272B at (906,437)) match the background. The only inner wall visible is the upper rail's brown band (#5F402F). The lower rail's inner wall and the back view can't be seen, so 'partial' is correct for a single view.

checks.claim: Invariant partial: substantial bridge
checks.reason: Same evidence as the bridge issue: a short, waisted, recessed strut.

checks.claim: Invariant partial: warm ivory/steel faces
checks.reason: The faces are broad and quiet, but the ivory median is #E6C8AB (peach). Cool steel appears only on the tip facets (#A6A0AB at (1470,20)).

checks.claim: Invariant partial: guard depth and overlap with blade base
checks.reason: The ivory root meets the red body along a diagonal butt line with a small bevel step. Nothing shows the guard wrapping the blade, and the pommel-side blocks are muddled.

checks.claim: Invariant partial: low amber along inner edges/channel
checks.reason: The heat is a localized bloom at the root only, with no channel.

checks.claim: Invariant partial: forged ivory, avoid noisy grunge
checks.reason: Bevels and tip facets are crisp. The cloud mottling on the faces is the weak point.

missed.fix: Decide explicitly: mirror the small lower spur (cleaner, the recommended route) and note that the large upper spur is being removed as an artifact. Or mirror the large one if the guard needs more pommel-side mass at icon size.

qc.overall: Sunbound does its main job. It reads at once as a solid, continuous broad sword with no fork or slot, and it sits clearly apart from Oathsplitter in silhouette. The gold sun disk is a real layered boss: raised rim, inner star, faceted gem center, and it sits on the junction of the guard arms. The cloth is short, cleanly rooted and clear of the grip. The main gaps are against the written brief. The broad face is painted warm peach-ivory, not the pearl steel the brief asks for. The vermilion spine is a hairline that disappears at icon size. The gold, especially the large bright pommel block, is warmer and louder than a restrained aged-gold accent. The face carries a baked camera-dependent hotspot. All of these can be fixed in modeling and texturing without redoing the concept.

invariants.requirement: "Create one solid broad sword with a continuous blade."
invariants.evidence: Single unbroken blade plate from the stepped root flare (~x540-860) to the tip (~1505,25). No openings, the face is uninterrupted, and it is broad, about 13% of total length wide.

invariants.requirement: "no fork, no long central slot, and no duplicated split-blade assembly" / must be visibly different from Oathsplitter
invariants.evidence: There is one symmetric spear-type point and no negative space anywhere in the blade. Next to 01_Oathsplitter.webp the twin rails and slot are absent, so the silhouettes separate at a glance.

invariants.requirement: "heavy, decisive cutting shape" / "decisive executioner-like shape" (concept brief)
invariants.evidence: Heavy and broad with near-parallel edges and a stepped root flare. The tip is a symmetric diamond/spear point (kinks at ~1255,60 and ~1370,197), which reads more as a broadsword than an executioner's squared or clipped head. Acceptable if this is the approved image.

invariants.requirement: "a broad quiet pearl-steel face"
invariants.evidence: The face is quiet, with no runes or noise. It is painted warm peach-ivory (sampled #D5BEA8 mid, #FAE2CC hotspot), well off pearl steel #C9CDD0. Only the edge bevels read cool (#F3E6E5 lit, #706366 shade).

invariants.requirement: "vermilion central spine/inlay concentrated near the blade root"
invariants.evidence: A red inlay comes out from under the disk at about 2 o'clock and tapers to a point near (880,385), roughly the first 30% of the exposed blade. Sampled #AB3833 / #933025.

invariants.requirement: "with a readable assembly relationship to the pale blade"
invariants.evidence: The inlay sits in a beveled groove and visibly continues from the red guard body under the disk, which is a plausible langet. It is only ~8-10 px wide on a ~220 px blade, and in the 64 px icon test it is a faint line, so the assembly does not read at distance.

invariants.requirement: "Keep the broad outer cutting perimeter pearl steel; do not add a full red outer-edge frame."
invariants.evidence: Both edge bevels and the tip facets are pale and cool. Red appears only on the guard, the inner inlay and the collars.

invariants.requirement: "a compact aged-gold sunburst-like disk the main focal ornament" near the guard
invariants.evidence: Circular disk about 9-10% of total length in diameter, centered on the guard hub (~565,540), with a 12-point star and radiating ivory relief rays on the blade root. It holds focus in both the full image and the icon test. The color is brighter and more orange than aged gold (#B6844F rim, #965723 star shade).

invariants.requirement: "mechanically attached, with a center, depth, and clear layering, rather than a flat oversized sticker"
invariants.evidence: Layers from back to front are red guard arms, then a raised gold rim with a beveled inner wall, then a recessed star field, then a faceted red gem center. The rim overlaps both arms and the blade root, and its cast shadow and thickness are visible on the lower-right side.

invariants.requirement: "Keep the perimeter simple enough to read at inventory size"
invariants.evidence: The outer rim is a plain circle. At 64x43 px the disk reads as a gold roundel with a red dot.

invariants.requirement: "Place small red or gold echoes elsewhere only where they connect the collection"
invariants.evidence: Red/gold collars at both ends of the grip are appropriate echoes. The pommel is a large faceted gold block with a bright #EEC385 highlight, a second gold mass rather than a small echo.

invariants.requirement: "short ivory cloth or seal streamer at a pommel attachment, clear of the hand grip"
invariants.evidence: An ivory streamer hangs from a gold loop and gold/red binding cap at the pommel butt (~45-80, 870-910). It flows below and away from the wrap and never crosses the grip.

invariants.requirement: "without becoming the main silhouette or covering the blade" / "Avoid ... an enormous tail"
invariants.evidence: About 24% of total length and about 4.5% wide, kept entirely in the lower-left corner, far from the blade.

invariants.requirement: "readable fabric width and a clean attachment ... a stable root, a controlled free end"
invariants.evidence: Root is gathered in a gold cylinder cap with a red band on a ring. The free end is a clean angled cut with a red chevron mark. There is one half-twist near the root.

invariants.requirement: "reasonable clearance from fingers and forearms"
invariants.evidence: The root is beyond the pommel, so it is clear of the hand at rest. Forearm clearance during swings cannot be judged from a static image and must be checked on the rig.

invariants.requirement: "effects ... concentrated around the guard disk and selected spine seams"
invariants.evidence: There is amber glow only at the lower 3-4 star points of the disk (~555-600, 575-590) and none on the spine seams. A stray orange spark floats at ~(465,465) beside the upper guard arm.

invariants.requirement: Shared: "Leave meaningful quiet surfaces. Concentrate detail at guards, connection points..."
invariants.evidence: Detail sits in the guard/disk/root-ray cluster and the pommel. The remaining ~70% of the blade face is clean.

invariants.requirement: "The dark usable grip separates the decorated guard from the pommel" / "Charcoal wraps should look grippable and less reflective"
invariants.evidence: Matte spiral leather wrap between red/gold collars. Value is clearly the darkest material (#211817-#3B2F31), although the hue is warm plum-brown rather than cool charcoal #24282D.

invariants.requirement: "Red elements are substantial structural pieces ... with visible thickness"
invariants.evidence: Guard arms and collars show chunky beveled thickness (lit #B0373D, shade #77150E). The spine inlay is too thin to read as a structural piece.

invariants.requirement: "Reserve the brightest highlights for important edges and focal materials" / painted highlights must not depend on one camera angle
invariants.evidence: The brightest large value in the image is a soft hotspot in the middle of the blade face (~1150,300, #FAE2CC), not an edge or the focal disk. It is camera-dependent lighting baked into the paint.

invariants.requirement: Section 7: hidden surfaces (rear, side, guard, grip, pommel) with intentional thickness and credible joints
invariants.evidence: Only one three-quarter front view is shown. Blade cross-section, guard depth, the rear of the disk and the pommel lug are not shown; resolutions are listed under ambiguities.

issues.where: Broad blade face, whole length (e.g. ~1000,380 and ~1250,200)
issues.problem: The face is warm peach-ivory (#D5BEA8 to #FAE2CC), not the brief's pearl steel #C9CDD0. Sunbound loses the cooler pearl identity that is meant to set its calm face apart, and it drifts toward Oathsplitter's warm ivory blade.
issues.fix: Texture the face as a pearl-ivory blend: base about #D3D1CB with cool pearl #C9CDD0 dominant toward the tip and edges, and keep warmth (#E5DDC7) only near the root rays. Keep the warm/cool contrast with the bevels, but make the face the cooler of the two family blades.

issues.where: Red spine inlay, from the disk at 2 o'clock to its tapered end near (880,385)
issues.problem: The inlay is a hairline, about 4% of blade width. It vanishes at inventory size and reads more as a painted stripe than an assembled part, which weakens a top-two priority ('pearl face versus red spine').
issues.fix: Model it as a separate inset strip, about 10-12% of blade width at the root, tapering to a point at about 35% of exposed blade length. Seat it in a V-channel with visible ivory bevel walls about 1.5x the strip width, raise it slightly proud of the channel floor, and run it under the disk into the guard body as one red langet piece. Mirror it on the rear face.

issues.where: Blade face hotspot around (1100-1200, 260-330)
issues.problem: A large soft specular bloom is baked into the paint and is the brightest value on the object. It competes with the focal disk and only works for this camera, which the brief forbids.
issues.fix: Do not paint it into the albedo. Use a broad, even face gradient (slightly lighter toward the spine, darker toward the inner bevel line) with edge-only highlights, and let the optional inspection sweep be a moving shader or VFX highlight.

issues.where: Pommel block (~40-150, 790-900) and all gold parts
issues.problem: The pommel is a big faceted gold mass with a near-cream highlight (#EEC385). All gold runs saturated orange (#B6844F, #965723) instead of the muted aged gold #9D7950, so at icon size there are two competing gold focal blobs at opposite ends.
issues.fix: Shrink the pommel by about 20% and make its main body red (#B93C2B) or dark steel, keeping gold to a faceted end cap and the loop, matching Oathsplitter's red-and-gold pommel logic. Desaturate all gold toward #9D7950 and reserve brighter gold only for the disk rim edge.

issues.problem: The wrap is short (about 16% of total length, versus about 22% on Oathsplitter) for such a broad, heavy blade. It is unclear whether this is one- or two-handed.
issues.fix: Decide the hold on the actual avatar. If it is two-handed, extend the wrap by about 25% (to about 20% of total length) and keep the blade length fixed. Keep the collars so the hand zone stays clearly bounded.

issues.where: Disk star points, lower-left only (~555-600, 575-590)
issues.problem: Amber glow appears only on the lower three or four star points. That is lighting-inconsistent and shows no 'selected spine seams' accent.
issues.fix: Treat the glow as emissive, not lighting. In idle, use a small even ring of low emission between the star points and around the gem. On reveal, brighten the disk briefly and run a short pulse along both edges of the red spine channel, then settle back.

issues.where: Floating spark left of the upper guard arm (~465,465)
issues.problem: A stray ember particle sits off the object with no source. It is either a generation artifact or unexplained VFX.
issues.fix: Ignore it for modeling. If sparks are wanted, emit them only from the disk during the reveal.

issues.where: Grip wrap color (#211817 to #3B2F31)
issues.problem: The wrap is warm plum-brown rather than cool charcoal #24282D, which reduces hue separation from the deep-red shadows of the collars (#77150E/#88231B).
issues.fix: Push the wrap base toward #2A2B2F with cool highlights around #4A4D52 and keep it low-roughness-contrast. Apply the same correction to Oathsplitter and Warlink so the family stays matched.

issues.where: Cloth marking, free end (~330-440, 880-990)
issues.problem: The red chevron and bracketed-diamond glyph is half-legible and could read as lettering. It is also detailed enough to draw the eye away from the disk.
issues.fix: Keep it as a texture-only mark. Simplify it to the chevron plus a single diamond, make sure it is an original glyph rather than text or a third-party mark, and keep it at about 70% opacity of the vermilion.

issues.where: Pommel loop attachment (~40-70, 860-910)
issues.problem: The gold ring comes out of a side facet of the pommel with no visible lug or eye, so the join is undefined.
issues.fix: Add a short eye lug on the pommel's end axis with a real through-hole, pass the ring through it, and hang the cloth cap from the ring. The ring stays rigid; the cloth bones start below the cap.

issues.where: Whole image versus 00_original_style_ref.webp
issues.problem: Rendering has moved from the reference's flat painterly planes, thin orange-red guard and slim handle to heavier glossy bevels and a crimson-leaning red. The drift is shared by all three new concepts, so the family is internally consistent.
issues.fix: No concept change. In texturing, warm the reds slightly toward vermilion (#B93C2B, with green above blue) and keep painted value blocks broad so the result sits between the original reference and the new concepts.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Only the front face is visible. It is unclear whether the face is flat, or has a central ridge or fuller, and how thick the blade is.
ambiguities.resolution: Use a flattened hexagon cross-section: a flat central face on both sides, edge bevels about 12% of width on each side ending in a blunt land (about 0.4% of total length, not knife-thin). Core thickness about 3% of total length at the root, tapering to about 2% near the tip. The red inlay channel is the only recess. The rear face mirrors the front, including the inlay and rays.

ambiguities.where: Ivory sun rays on the blade root around the disk
ambiguities.ambiguity: It is unclear whether the rays are geometry, shallow relief or texture, and whether they repeat on the back.
ambiguities.resolution: Model them as shallow relief (about 0.5% of total length) beveled into the blade root on both faces, around 10 rays radiating from the disk center. Bake to normal maps if the triangle budget needs it. Do not add further rays elsewhere on the blade.

ambiguities.where: Disk, gem and guard on the rear side
ambiguities.ambiguity: It is unclear whether the disk and gem appear on both faces, and how they mount to the guard and tang.
ambiguities.resolution: Make the guard one red body with a central hub that has a slot for the blade tang. Mount a gold disk boss on each face of the hub, with a matching star and gem on the rear (or a plain star with a gold boss on the rear if the budget is tight). Disk thickness is about 1.5% of total length per side, the rim stands about 0.6% proud, and the gem is a separate low-poly faceted mesh for emissive control.

ambiguities.where: Guard arm depth and swallowtail ends
ambiguities.ambiguity: Arm thickness along the blade axis is not shown, and it is unclear whether the V-notched ends are flat or beveled.
ambiguities.resolution: Make the arms about 1.3x blade core thickness with a chamfered top and bottom. Each arm ends in a two-point swallowtail with a concave V notch about 30% of arm width. Inset the gold chevron trims as separate thin strips about 0.3% of length proud of the arm surface, on both faces.

ambiguities.ambiguity: It is unclear whether the ivory blade root passes through the guard or sits on its face.
ambiguities.resolution: Insert the blade root into the guard slot so the stepped root flare overlaps the guard by about 2% of total length on both faces. The red spine inlay is continuous with the guard hub as one part, which gives a readable langet. The tang continues hidden through the collars into the grip core.

ambiguities.ambiguity: How the ring attaches, the shape of the pommel's rear facets, and where the cloth root sits relative to the grip axis.
ambiguities.resolution: Use a faceted octagonal pommel with an end eye lug on the grip axis, a rigid gold ring through the lug, and a rigid gold cap with a red band crimping the cloth. Cloth is a separate mesh about 24% of total length and 4.5% wide, 6-8 bone chain, with the first bone parented rigidly to the cap. Remove the baked half-twist from the rest pose and let any twist come from simulation.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Is the grip round or oval, and is the wrap geometry or texture?
ambiguities.resolution: Use a slightly oval cylinder (about 3.3% of total length in diameter, oval along the edge plane to show blade orientation by feel). The spiral wrap is a shallow modeled ridge every 2-3 bands at most, with the rest done in normal and albedo maps.

ambiguities.ambiguity: One- or two-handed, and the absolute size in Roblox.
ambiguities.resolution: Set scale against the avatar rig: blade about 62% of total length (measured from the disk center), guard span about 20%, wrap about 16-20%, pommel and collars about 10%. Put the grip pivot at the upper third of the wrap and check two-hand fit before locking the wrap length.

strengths: Clear silhouette difference from Oathsplitter: solid continuous broad blade with no negative space, recognizable even in a 64 px icon test.
The disk is a convincing layered mechanical boss with a plain round rim, inner star, faceted gem and visible rim thickness, not a sticker.
Large quiet blade face with detail concentrated at the guard, root rays and pommel, which matches the shared art direction.
Strong value grouping: light blade, mid red/gold guard, dark grip, light cloth, with clear material boundaries at every collar.
The broad outer cutting perimeter is kept pale and cool with no red edge frame, as the brief requires.
The cloth is well scoped: short, attached by a clean cap-and-ring root beyond the hand zone, with a controlled angled free end that never crosses the blade or grip.
Family consistency with 01 and 03: same red/gold/ivory/dark-wrap language, collar treatment and presentation angle.

parts.name: SB_Blade
parts.material: pearl-ivory forged metal (face) with cooler pearl-steel edge bevels
parts.shape: Straight broad plate with near-parallel edges, a stepped two-notch root flare (wings) and a symmetric diamond spear point over the last ~15% of length. Flattened hexagon cross-section with flat faces, ~12% bevels and a blunt edge land. Shallow ray relief around the disk on both faces, plus a V-channel for the spine inlay.
parts.approx_proportion: About 62% of total length (from disk center to tip). Width about 13% of length, about 16% at the root flare. Core thickness about 3% of length at the root tapering to about 2% at the tip.

parts.name: SB_SpineInlay
parts.material: vermilion enamel/forged red
parts.shape: Tapered strip seated in a beveled V-channel along the centerline, continuous with the guard hub under the disk. Mirrored on the rear face.
parts.approx_proportion: Runs the first ~35% of exposed blade. About 10-12% of blade width at the root, tapering to a point. Stands about 0.3% of length proud of the channel floor.

parts.name: SB_Guard
parts.material: vermilion forged metal with inset aged-gold chevron trim strips
parts.shape: Crossguard hub with two arms perpendicular to the blade, each ending in a V-notched swallowtail with two points. Chamfered edges. A slot receives the blade tang.
parts.approx_proportion: Span about 20% of total length perpendicular to the blade. Arm width about 5%. Thickness about 1.3x blade core (about 4% of length).

parts.name: SB_SunDisk
parts.material: aged gold (rim and star) and red faceted gem center (emissive-capable)
parts.shape: Round boss on each face of the guard hub: plain raised beveled rim, recessed 12-point star field, faceted hexagonal-dome gem center as a separate mesh.
parts.approx_proportion: Diameter about 9-10% of total length. About 1.5% thick per side, rim about 0.6% proud. Gem about 35% of disk diameter.

parts.name: SB_Collars
parts.material: vermilion bands with aged-gold rings
parts.shape: Two stacked beveled cylinder rings at the top of the grip (below the disk) and two at the bottom (above the pommel).
parts.approx_proportion: Each set about 3% of length long and about 1.3x grip diameter.

parts.name: SB_Grip
parts.material: charcoal leather wrap, matte
parts.shape: Slightly oval cylinder with spiral overlapping wrap bands. Ridges are mostly normal-mapped, with a few modeled.
parts.approx_proportion: About 16% of length (extend to about 20% if two-handed is confirmed). Diameter about 3.3% of length.

parts.name: SB_Pommel
parts.material: vermilion body with aged-gold faceted end cap (recommended shift from the all-gold image)
parts.shape: Faceted octagonal nut tapering to a gold cap, with an end eye lug on the grip axis.
parts.approx_proportion: About 5% of length long and about 4.5% wide (about 20% smaller than drawn).

parts.name: SB_ClothRing
parts.material: aged gold
parts.shape: Rigid torus through the pommel lug, plus a small gold cylinder cap with a red band crimping the cloth root.
parts.approx_proportion: Ring outer diameter about 2.5% of length. Cap about 2% long.

parts.name: SB_Cloth
parts.material: ivory cloth (two-sided), with a vermilion chevron and diamond mark as texture only
parts.shape: Single ribbon strip, slightly widening, with an angled cut free end. Separate mesh with a 6-8 bone chain whose root bone is locked to the cap. Rest pose is flat with no baked twist.
parts.approx_proportion: About 24% of total length, about 4.5% wide, cloth thickness about 0.3% (or a two-sided plane with a small solidify).

sampled_palette: Blade face recommended target: #D3D1CB (pearl #C9CDD0 / ivory #E5DDC7 blend)
Cloth red mark: #B16B5B to #C29D84 (painted, semi-transparent read)
build_spec.notes: The image is a single three-quarter front view; every rear and side surface is inferred above. Hex values are point-averaged samples from the webp under the image's warm studio lighting. Under neutral light, correct toward the brief swatches: cool the face toward pearl, shift reds slightly toward vermilion (green above blue), desaturate gold toward #9D7950, and cool the wrap toward #24282D. Separate objects for emissive and animation: SB_SunDisk gem and star emissive mask, SB_SpineInlay channel-edge emissive mask, SB_Cloth with its bone chain. Effects-off must still read through mesh alone: inlay width and disk rim depth carry the read, not glow. Keep the stray spark and the lower-only star glow out of the model.

checks.claim: Invariant 'executioner-like shape' partial: tip is a symmetric spear/diamond point, not a squared executioner head
checks.reason: Tip is a symmetric chisel-diamond point with kinks at about (1255,60) and (1370,197). Edges are near-parallel and the body is heavy, but the head is pointed, not squared or clipped.

checks.claim: Invariant 'pearl-steel face' partial / Issue: face is warm peach-ivory, not pearl steel
checks.reason: I re-sampled (1000,380) = #D5BEA8 and (1250,200) = #FAE2CC. The face is clearly warm peach. Only the bevels read cool (upper bevel #FBF4F4). Medium severity is fair, since 'pearl face vs red spine' is priority two.

checks.claim: Invariant 'readable assembly relationship' partial / Issue: inlay is a hairline that vanishes at icon size and reads as a painted stripe
checks.reason: Width is confirmed at about 6-8 px on a 200-230 px blade (3-4%), widening to about 20 px where it leaves the disk. But in the zoomed guard crop it clearly sits in a beveled channel with lit and shaded walls, and it runs under the disk into the red guard. At a 64x43 downsample it still shows as a distinct red line. The proposed 10-12% width roughly triples what the brief calls 'as shown in the approved image'. A modest widening (about 1.5x) plus mirroring on the rear is enough.

checks.claim: Invariant 'small red or gold echoes' partial / Issue: pommel is a big all-gold mass competing with the disk; fix is to make the pommel body red with only a gold end cap
checks.reason: The pommel crop shows the pommel is already two-part: a red faceted body next to the lower collar (sample (140,800) = #C34044) and a gold faceted end cap. The recommended fix is essentially what is drawn, and the build_spec note 'shift from the all-gold image' is factually wrong. What remains true: the gold cap is large and brighter and more orange than #9D7950. At icon size it shows as a small gold blob, much weaker than the disk.

checks.claim: Invariant forearm clearance partial (cannot judge from a static image)
checks.reason: The cloth roots below the end cap, beyond the wrap. Swing clearance needs a rig test.

checks.claim: Invariant effects partial / Issue: glow only on the lower star points, none on spine seams
checks.reason: The guard crop shows amber glow on only the bottom three star points of the disk. No glow anywhere along the spine channel.

checks.claim: Invariant 'red elements are substantial structural pieces' partial: spine too thin
checks.reason: Guard arms and collars are chunky and beveled. The spine is thin but has visible channel walls and a faceted tapered tip, so it reads as an inset part, not a stroke.

checks.claim: Invariant highlights partial / Issue: the face hotspot is the brightest large value in the image, not an edge
checks.reason: A soft baked bloom around (1150-1250, 200-300) is real (#FDEDD9 at (1180,260)) and camera-dependent, so the fix is valid. But the upper edge bevel is brighter (#FBF4F4 at (1100,180), higher sum), so the claim that it is brighter than the edges is wrong. It competes by area, not by peak value.

checks.claim: Invariant section 7 hidden surfaces partial (single 3/4 view)
checks.reason: There is only one front three-quarter view. Rear, side and cross-section are not shown.

checks.claim: Issue: grip wrap short (about 16%), hold unclear
checks.reason: The wrap runs between the collars at about (170,770) and (430,630), about 295 px of about 1696 px total, so about 17%. Room for roughly one and a half hands, and the hold must be decided on the rig.

checks.claim: Issue: stray orange spark at about (465,465)
checks.reason: An isolated orange dot sits left of the upper guard arm (#CE975D at (470,462)) with no source geometry.

checks.claim: Issue: wrap is warm plum-brown, not cool charcoal
checks.reason: The wrap samples #5C4E51 to #645658 lit and is visibly purple-brown in the crop. Low severity is right.

qc.overall: Warlink works as a compact paired-cleaver concept. The two broad ivory cleavers with red spine housings, charcoal wraps and a short, thick, properly alternating chain clearly fit the family, and the silhouette reads well at inventory size and differs from both long swords. The weak spot is the feature the brief calls its focal detail. There is no real pommel: each grip ends in a plain red ferrule, and the steel eyelet ring simply disappears behind it, so the eyelet-to-pommel join is neither credible nor emphasized. Smaller fixes: the cutting bevel is ambiguous, the quiet state has no amber accent, the dark warm chain sits too close to the background value, and edge-on links look thicker than face-on links. A modeler can resolve all of these without redrawing the concept.

invariants.requirement: "a matching pair of short, broad cleavers"
invariants.evidence: Two nearly mirror-image cleavers (left-right pixel mirror difference is only about 9/255 on average). Each blade is broad: maximum width is about 47% of blade length and about 29% of total cleaver length. Blades are short relative to the long swords.

invariants.requirement: "connected through robust pommel eyelets by a thick dark-steel chain"
invariants.evidence: A thick dark-steel chain joins the two grip ends through large steel rings. But there is no pommel body: the grip ends in a red ferrule band, and the eyelet ring's top is hidden behind that band with no lug, tang or loop-through shown.

invariants.requirement: "Treat the pair and chain as one weapon concept"
invariants.evidence: A single symmetric composition. The chain hangs in a U between the two pommels and both cleavers point outward and up.

invariants.requirement: "fit the same heroic ivory/red family while providing a compact, aggressive alternative to the long swords"
invariants.evidence: Same ivory faces, red structural parts, charcoal cross-wrap and red collar/ferrule rings as Oathsplitter and Sunbound. Short, wide, hooked shapes give a clearly different silhouette.

invariants.requirement: "small split or notched outer-tip motif, but must not become miniature copies of Oathsplitter's long opening"
invariants.evidence: A single V-notch at the outer tip forms a tall outer prong and a shorter inner prong. The notch is only about 10-12% of blade length deep and is not an enclosed slot.

invariants.requirement: "substantial ivory cutting faces, red spine or guard components, charcoal grips, and restrained gold connection details"
invariants.evidence: Large quiet ivory faces. A red U-shaped spine housing runs the full inner edge into a red guard with one hooked quillon. Grips are charcoal cross-wrapped. Gold is limited to one rivet, a forked inlay along the spine, and two brass connector rings at the chain ends.

invariants.requirement: "Give each blade a real cutting bevel"
invariants.evidence: The outer edge shows a light grey band of constant width from tip to heel, squared off at the heel. It could be a wide primary bevel seen in 3/4 view, or just a flat slab side. Nothing in the image shows it converging to an edge.

invariants.requirement: "coherent side thickness"
invariants.evidence: Side and bevel planes are visible along the outer edges. The notch interior shows wall thickness. The red spine housing has a darker side facet and stands proud of the ivory.

invariants.requirement: "a clear gripping zone"
invariants.evidence: The charcoal wrap is bracketed by a red collar at the guard and a red ferrule at the end, about 24% of cleaver length, which is one-hand sized.

invariants.requirement: "Place chain eyelets beyond the grip so links do not pass through the fingers"
invariants.evidence: The eyelet rings sit entirely below the red ferrule. No link overlaps the wrap.

invariants.requirement: "Build eyelets as physical loops with visible interior thickness"
invariants.evidence: The eyelet has an open center (inner diameter about 0.07 of cleaver length) with a visibly shaded inner wall and chamfered faces.

invariants.requirement: "credible connection to the pommels"
invariants.evidence: The ring's upper arc just goes behind the red ferrule. No hole, lug or weld shows how a closed ring enters a solid end cap.

invariants.requirement: "links must look like rigid interlocking metal pieces... alternate their orientation... preserve their open centers"
invariants.evidence: 9 links: 5 face-on links with open centers alternate with 4 edge-on bars, and each bar passes through the neighbouring face-on openings. Links are chamfered and hard-edged.

invariants.requirement: "Keep link dimensions consistent"
invariants.evidence: Outer lengths are roughly consistent, but edge-on links show a cross-section about 40 px across, while face-on rims are about 25 px wide. Edge-on links therefore read about 1.5x thicker than the same link seen face-on.

invariants.requirement: "Bend the chain through the changing relationship between links, rather than visibly stretching"
invariants.evidence: A smooth U curve made from changing link angles. No stretched or elongated links.

invariants.requirement: "Avoid per-link decorative noise"
invariants.evidence: Only small edge nicks and chamfer highlights per link. No engravings.

invariants.requirement: "compact chain length... not a long-range whip"
invariants.evidence: The arc from eyelet to eyelet is about 1.0x one cleaver's length (9 steel links plus 2 brass connectors). The span between eyelets at rest is about 0.75x cleaver length. This image defines the canonical length.

invariants.requirement: "Use local amber heat near a few links, connection points, or blade seams" / quiet state "Local endpoint/link heat"
invariants.evidence: No amber anywhere. The faint warm-orange rim on the lower edges of the links reads as rim light, not heat. Both sibling concepts show a small amber accent in their quiet state.

invariants.requirement: Shared art direction (section 3): quiet surfaces, detail concentrated at guards and joints, red parts substantial with visible thickness, charcoal wraps less reflective
invariants.evidence: The ivory faces are broad and mostly empty. Detail sits at the spine housing, guard, collar and connectors. The red parts have chunky bevels. The wrap is matte.

invariants.requirement: Section 3: "Ivory metal should still read as forged material"
invariants.evidence: Clean bevels and edge brightness are present, but the face has blotchy, veined patches that read slightly like marble or chalk rather than forged metal.

invariants.requirement: Section 16: "Warlink visibly contains two cleavers joined at their pommels"
invariants.evidence: Reads immediately, including at a 96x64 icon downsample.

invariants.requirement: Section 7: front, rear, side, guard, grip, pommel surfaces with intentional thickness; inspect eyelet negative space from several angles
invariants.evidence: Only one 3/4 front view is given. The back faces, the guard's back side, the top of the eyelet under the ferrule and the blade cross-section are not shown (resolved in ambiguities).

issues.where: Grip ends of both cleavers, where the red ferrule meets the steel eyelet ring (about x 400-520, y 690-830 on the left; mirrored on the right)
issues.problem: There is no pommel, and the eyelet's attachment cannot be built as drawn. A closed steel ring disappears behind a solid red ferrule band with no lug, slot or loop-through, so the stated invariant 'credible connection to the pommels' is not resolved. This joint is also the concept's listed focal detail.
issues.fix: Add a real pommel cap below the ferrule: a short faceted red/gold block, about 0.07 L long, that tapers into a forged steel lug. Make the eyelet one rigid piece with that lug (a fixed loop with a visible weld or collar), oriented in the blade plane. The brass ring becomes the first moving piece. Keep the eyelet's outer diameter about 0.15 L and inner diameter about 0.07 L.

issues.where: Pommel eyelets versus chain links (focal hierarchy)
issues.problem: The comparative table lists 'Pommel eyelets and blade connections' as Warlink's focal detail. In the image the eyelets are the same dark brown-grey steel and almost the same size as the chain links, so they read as just the first link. The eye goes to the ivory blades and red spine instead.
issues.fix: Separate the eyelet from the links: give the pommel lug a gold or red collar band, add a slightly brighter steel bevel highlight on the eyelet, and place the quiet-state amber heat at this joint (see amber issue). Keep the links plain.

issues.where: Outer cutting edge of both blades (the light grey band along the outer side, about 30-40 px wide)
issues.problem: The band is the same width from tip to heel and squared at the heel, so it could be a cutting bevel or a flat slab side. The brief asks for a 'real cutting bevel'. If modeled literally as a flat side, the blade will have a blunt square edge.
issues.fix: Model it as a flat-ground primary bevel on both faces, each about 15-18% of blade width, meeting at a small microflat (about 0.004 L). Let the bevel narrow slightly into the heel corner instead of ending square, and add a brighter thin edge highlight on the apex in texture.

issues.where: Whole chain plus charcoal grips against the background (chain mid about #4A403C, wrap about #473934, background #262324)
issues.problem: Value grouping: the warm, dark chain is only about one value step above the dark background, and it shares hue and value with the grip wrap. In the downsampled icon the chain becomes a faint dotted arc, and in Roblox scenes with dark floors it will disappear.
issues.fix: Shift chain steel cooler and slightly lighter (base about #4C5056, chamfer highlight about #A9AFB5) so it reads as steel rather than the warm charcoal leather (keep the wrap at about #2E2A2C to #3A3234). Preserve the bright chamfer edge highlights on each link and keep the link interiors darker (about #1E2023).

issues.where: Chain, the 4 edge-on links (centered roughly at x 640, 745 and mirrored, y 880-960)
issues.problem: Edge-on links show a cross-section about 1.5x wider than the rim of face-on links, so as drawn they are two different link sizes. Built literally, this breaks 'keep link dimensions consistent'.
issues.fix: Use one link mesh for all 9 links: outer about 0.14 L x 0.10 L, a single wire section about 0.035 L, a chamfered octagonal profile, and 90 degree alternation. Ignore the drawn thickness difference.

issues.where: Quiet effect state (entire concept)
issues.problem: No amber at all, while the brief's quiet state calls for 'local endpoint/link heat' and both sibling concepts carry a small amber accent.
issues.fix: Add a small amber (#F5AB46) emissive seam where the eyelet meets the pommel lug, and optionally a faint heat tint on the 1-2 links next to each end. Limit the bloom so the link gaps stay readable. The activation pulse along the chain stays an effect-state feature.

issues.where: Ivory blade faces, mid and lower blade near the inlay
issues.problem: Blotchy, veined paint patches read slightly like marble or chalk rather than forged metal. Overall the ivory is warmer and peachier (lit about #E8D1BC, mid about #D0B198) than the warm ivory swatch #E5DDC7, and the outer bevel is warm grey (#A2918D) rather than pearl steel #C9CDD0.
issues.fix: Texture with broad, low-frequency face variation aligned along the blade length, a cooler pearl-steel bevel (about #C9CDD0 lit, #8E9296 shade), and darker inner edges near the spine. Pull the face toward #E5DDC7 / #CFC3A8 and drop the vein-like streaks.

issues.where: Red guard and spine housing on both cleavers
issues.problem: Family detail mismatch: the sibling guards carry gold trim lines or inlays on the red, while Warlink's guard is plain red and its gold sits on the blade. The red pieces also have lightning-like marbled specular streaks (most visible on the collars and ferrules) that read as glossy marble.
issues.fix: Add a thin aged-gold (#9D7950) edge trim on the guard's front bevel or the ferrule (one band only, to stay restrained). Replace marbled streaks with soft broad enamel highlights on the bevels.

issues.where: Lighting across the pair
issues.problem: The near-mirrored composition is also mirror-lit (left cleaver lit from the upper left, right cleaver from the upper right). This is fine for a presentation sheet but not from one light source, and it hides which faces are the real front.
issues.fix: None needed in the concept. In Blender, review both cleavers under one neutral key light, plus the front, rear and side views required by section 16.

ambiguities.ambiguity: The back sides are never shown: does the red spine housing, gold rivet and forked gold inlay also appear on the back?
ambiguities.resolution: Make the blade symmetric about its center plane. The red spine housing is a U-channel that wraps the spine and shows on both faces. The rivet is a through-rivet with a domed head on both sides. The gold inlay is repeated on the back as shallow relief (about 0.002 L).

ambiguities.ambiguity: Blade thickness, and whether the outer band is a bevel or a flat side.
ambiguities.resolution: Spine/flat thickness about 0.035 L (L = overall cleaver length from tip to eyelet bottom). Flat-ground bevels about 15-18% of blade width per face, meeting at a small microflat on the outer edge. The red housing stands about 0.008 L proud of the ivory on each face.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Notch depth and how the two prongs end in thickness.
ambiguities.resolution: A V-notch about 0.07 L deep, starting about 0.25 of blade width in from the outer edge. Both prongs keep full blade thickness, with the bevel carried around the outer prong tip only. The notch walls are flat and visible from both sides.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Quillon plane, thickness, and whether the guard has a matching horn on the edge side.
ambiguities.resolution: The guard is a red block band about 0.06 L thick through its depth (about 1.7x blade thickness), wrapping the blade heel. One hooked quillon on the spine side only, in the blade plane, curling toward the tip and projecting about 0.12 L. The edge side ends flush with the blade heel, as drawn.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Are the cleavers identical or mirrored?
ambiguities.resolution: Use one source mesh plus a mirrored copy (Warlink_L / Warlink_R), so spines and quillons face inward toward the chain center in the rest pose, matching the image. Avoid mirrored UVs where text or asymmetric decals would flip (there are none here).

ambiguities.where: Eyelet attachment and orientation (hidden under the ferrule)
ambiguities.ambiguity: How the eyelet enters the pommel, and which plane the ring lies in.
ambiguities.resolution: Add a pommel cap with a steel lug. The eyelet is a fixed, rigid loop (part of the pommel object or a welded child), and its plane matches the blade plane (it appears face-on alongside the blade faces). The brass connector is the first free-moving piece. The attachment point is the eyelet's inner bottom, kept fixed relative to the grip.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Whether they are separate links or decoration.
ambiguities.resolution: Treat them as real chain links: smaller oval rings in aged-gold metal (about 0.11 x 0.075 L, wire about 0.028 L), passing through the eyelet and link 1, rotated 90 degrees relative to the eyelet.

ambiguities.where: Chain link count, cross-section and rest pose
ambiguities.ambiguity: Exact number of links and link profile.
ambiguities.resolution: Fixed 9 dark-steel links plus 2 brass connectors (13 pieces counting the eyelets), never added to or stretched. Chamfered octagonal wire section. At rest the chain hangs in a U whose lowest point is about 0.28 L below the eyelets, with the eyelets about 0.75 L apart.

ambiguities.where: Grip cross-section and wrap on the hidden side
ambiguities.ambiguity: Round versus oval grip, and wrap pattern continuity.
ambiguities.resolution: Slightly oval cylinder (about 0.095 L across the blade plane, 0.085 L through it). The cross-wrap continues helically around the back. Wrap relief goes in the normal or height map, with only a shallow geometric bump for the silhouette.

ambiguities.where: Red spine housing top cap and stepped notch
ambiguities.ambiguity: How the housing ends at the tip, and the depth of the step near the lower third.
ambiguities.resolution: The housing ends in an angled pointed cap flush with the blade's top edge. The step is a 0.02 L inward jog in the housing's inner edge only. The outer spine line stays straight.

strengths: Clear, distinct silhouette: two compact hooked cleavers plus a U-shaped chain read immediately, even at a 96x64 icon downsample, and cannot be confused with Oathsplitter or Sunbound.
The chain is well built: 9 rigid chamfered links alternating face-on and edge-on with open centers, bending through link angles rather than stretching, with no per-link decorative noise.
The chain length is compact and well defined (about 1.0x cleaver length), giving a canonical tether length for animation.
Eyelets sit fully beyond the grip, so links never cross the hand zone, and the gripping zone is clearly framed by a red collar and ferrule.
The tip notch is a restrained family echo of Oathsplitter's split, not a miniature copy.

Good material hierarchy on the blades: large quiet ivory faces, substantial red spine and guard parts with visible thickness, matte charcoal wrap, and gold limited to a rivet, one directional inlay and two connector rings.

Strong family consistency with 01 and 02 in shapes (collar/ferrule rings, cross-wrap, hooked red guard forms) and painting style. It also keeps the original reference's ivory-blade / red-hilt house identity.

sampled_palette: Outer bevel / side plane (sampled, warm grey): #A2918D

Recommended build targets: ivory #E5DDC7 / shade #CFC3A8; bevel pearl steel #C9CDD0 / shade #8E9296; vermilion #B93C2B; deep red #702D27; charcoal wrap #2E2A2C; aged gold #9D7950; chain steel #4C5056 / highlight #A9AFB5; amber accent #F5AB46
build_spec.notes: Composition: two nearly mirror-image cleavers, tips outward and up, joined at their grip ends by a U-shaped chain. Treat this image as canonical for chain length (9 steel links + 2 brass connectors + 2 fixed eyelets). Required departures from the drawing: (1) add a pommel cap and lug so the eyelet is a credible rigid loop; (2) one consistent link size, ignoring the thicker-looking edge-on links; (3) a real flat-ground cutting bevel on the outer edge; (4) cooler, slightly lighter chain steel to separate it from the warm charcoal wrap and dark backgrounds; (5) a small amber emissive seam at the eyelet/pommel joint for the quiet state. Suggested object names: Warlink_Blade_L/R (blade, housing, rivet and inlay merged, with material slots), Warlink_Hilt_L/R (guard, collar, grip, ferrule, pommel, eyelet), Warlink_Ring_L/R (brass), Warlink_Link_01..09 (instances of one mesh), or link bones on a curve rig. Pivots: each hilt at the grip center for equipping; chain endpoints at the eyelet's inner bottom. Keep the eyelets as part of the hilt so the attachment points cannot drift.

checks.claim: HIGH issue: no pommel; the closed eyelet ring disappears behind the red ferrule with no lug, slot or loop-through, so the connection cannot be built as drawn
checks.reason: Zooming into both grip ends (about x 410-530, y 700-800 on the left, mirrored on the right) shows a clear faceted hexagonal dark-steel lug/tang hanging from the bottom of the stepped red ferrule. It sits inside the top of the ring's opening and covers the ring's upper arc, so the ring reads as threaded through the lug. The connection is drawn and is buildable as a tang lug with a cross-hole. What is true: there is no distinct pommel mass. Both siblings have a faceted gold/red pommel, while Warlink ends in a plain two-tier red ferrule. This is medium at most (family consistency and focal emphasis), not a high 'cannot be built'. The fix should keep the drawn hex lug and pierce it for the ring, not invent a new 0.07 L pommel block plus lug that changes the silhouette.

checks.claim: Invariant 'connected through robust pommel eyelets' = partial
checks.reason: The rings are thick, chamfered, open-centered and joined through a visible steel lug at the end cap. The only shortfall is that the 'pommel' is a ferrule rather than a sculpted pommel. This is closer to 'yes, minor'.

checks.claim: Invariant 'credible connection to the pommels' = partial; 'ring's upper arc just goes behind the red ferrule, no hole, lug or weld'
checks.reason: A lug is plainly visible: a hex-faceted steel block between the ferrule's lower rim and the ring's inner top, on both cleavers. The evidence text misdescribes the image. The only thing unshown is the hole through the lug, which is normal for a 3/4 view and belongs in ambiguities.

checks.claim: MEDIUM: eyelets are the same steel and nearly the same size as the links, so they read as just the first link and the focal detail is weak
checks.reason: The eyelets are about 123 px across against face-on links about 110 px long, in the same warm dark steel (#4E413D range). They are only separated by being rounder and thicker. Nothing (no gold, no heat, no pommel mass) pulls the eye to the joint that the comparative table names as focal. The suggested fixes (collar band, amber seam) are reasonable.

checks.claim: MEDIUM: the outer grey band is constant width and squared, so it is ambiguous whether it is a bevel or a flat slab side
checks.reason: The outer edge shows a wide cool mauve-grey plane (lit about #D2C3BF to about #796C6C in shade), about 40-50 px wide on a blade about 250 px wide, constant from the tip prong to the heel, with a hard corner at the top. observations.what_happens: This is a screen recording of an X/Twitter feed in a desktop browser, not the weapon clip. The media viewer is open. A gold trident-headed spear is shown on a dark teal gradient background. The head points left and slightly up, and the butt points right and slightly down. A pale ribbon with a pastel pink/blue mottled pattern coils around the shaft from just behind the trident collar to the butt, then leaves the shaft as a free tail that bends upward and hooks down.

The trident head, shaft angle and screen position match in all three tiles. Near the head the coils are tight, narrow and close to the shaft. Coil width and distance from the shaft grow toward the butt. The free tail is a tall, broad loop rising up and right at 3.5, swings below the shaft at 3.833, and is back up as a loop at 4.167.

The tail probably makes a continuous up-down swing between these samples. With about 0.33 s between stills, the exact path, speed, easing and the number of swings between samples are unknown, and the motion could be aliased.

The embedded player has a progress bar and a time readout. Enlarged, the readout appears to say about '0:00 / 0:03' at 3.5 s and about '0:01 / 0:03' at 4.0 s. This suggests the source post is roughly a 3 s looping clip. The text is blurry and can't be confirmed exactly.

At 5.167 it forms a tall loop rising high above the shaft past the butt, and the gold pointed butt spike shows below it. At 5.5 the tail is still a tall upright loop that hangs down at its end. At 5.833 it whips down and right, ending in a thin pointed tip below and behind the butt. Across every sample the spear stays put: same screen position and angle, no visible translation or rotation. Only the ribbon changes. Small changes in roll or position would not be visible at this tile size.

The ribbon shapes at 3.0 and 6.0 look very similar (tail loop rising up and right past the butt). With an apparent clip length of about 3 s, this fits a seamless loop. Whether the motion truly repeats exactly can't be confirmed from two stills.
